content_preview.title: Valve's Steam Machine Launches at $1,049 on June 30 as a Reservation Lottery Replaces Preorders
content_preview.summary: Valve's cube-shaped SteamOS console shipped June 30 in four configurations from $1,049, sold through a randomized reservation lottery, with the company blaming an AI-driven memory shortage for a price far above its original target.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

Valve's revived Steam Machine has finally shipped. Both versions of the compact, cube-shaped SteamOS console were scheduled to launch on June 30, according to [Notebookcheck](https://www.notebookcheck.net/Steam-Machine-release-date-and-price-officially-confirmed.1326720.0.html), with the base model starting at $1,049, as [Engadget](https://www.engadget.com/2199144/valve-steam-machine-starts-at-1049-with-512gb-storage-and-no-controller/) reported. The launch closes a saga The Machine...

editor_notes.content_quality: Well-structured launch report (659 words, News category). Clear sectioning (Overview, Pricing, What's Inside, Why It Costs This Much, Critical Reception, What We Don't Know). Appropriate technical depth on the hardware SKUs and DRAM-supply context, with honest scoping of open questions.
editor_notes.source_verification: All 5 source snapshots read from disk and verified (all HTTP 200, no archive fallback). source-0 (Engadget): CONFIRMS four-tier pricing $1,049/$1,128/$1,349/$1,428, 512GB/2TB, June 25 1PM ET signup cutoff, June 29 purchase emails, April 27 prior-purchase requirement, good-standing + one-per-household rule, the verbatim 'tends to reward bots, people with fast internet connections' quote, ~six-inch cube, and connectivity (Bluetooth 5.3, Wi-Fi 6E, DisplayPort 1.4, HDMI 2.0). Does NOT contain the words 'SteamOS' or 'Linux' — the article's 'runs SteamOS, the same Linux-based operating system as the Steam Deck, according to Engadget' is misattributed (the fact is true and is stated by GamersNexus). source-1 (Notebookcheck): CONFIRMS June 30 launch date, $1,049 base, $99.99 standalone controller, June 25 registration cutoff, and the verbatim lottery quote 'Valve will randomly select buyers and notify them by email.' source-2 (GamersNexus): CONFIRMS all specs verbatim (6C/12T Zen 4, 4.8 GHz boost, 30W TDP, RDNA 3, 28 CUs, 2.45 GHz, 110W TDP, 8GB GDDR6, 16GB DDR5-5600) and the DRAM quote; also supports the AI/data-center memory-shortage framing ('The companies getting priority are NVIDIA, OpenAI, and other hyperscalers and data center companies'). source-3 (XDA): CONFIRMS $1,049-vs-$750-target and the RAM-market cause, but does NOT mention 'AI data-center demand' nor a '30 percent' figure. source-4 (PCGamesN): CONFIRMS IGN 8/10 (Jacqueline Thomas), The Verge 6/10 (Sean Hollister), and the PS5/Xbox-Series-X-are-cheaper value critique.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Headline and summary are fully sourced: June 30 launch, $1,049 base, four configurations, randomized reservation lottery, AI-driven memory shortage, and above-target pricing all trace to cited snapshots. Three subordinate-body discrepancies filed as corrections: (1) 'roughly 30 percent higher' is inaccurate — $750 to $1,049 is ~40 percent, and no cited source states 30 percent; (2) 'driven largely by AI data-center demand ... according to XDA Developers' is misattributed — XDA cites the RAM market generally; the AI/data-center causation is actually supported by GamersNexus; (3) 'runs SteamOS ... according to Engadget' is misattributed — Engadget's snapshot omits SteamOS/Linux; the detail is in GamersNexus. The DRAM quote silently drops the verbal filler 'they are, you know,' from the GamersNexus transcript but preserves meaning verbatim otherwise — acceptable filler cleanup, noted here rather than filed.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and professional. No sensationalism, no AI self-reference. Value criticism is attributed to reviewers, not editorialized.
editor_notes.originality: Genuine new substance, not a rehash. Ran as a force-follow-up to March (2026-03/10 recommit + pricing rethink) and May (2026-05/22 Steam Frame) coverage, both correctly linked as prior context. The new material dominates: the actual June 30 ship, the confirmed four-tier pricing, the reservation-lottery mechanic, Valve's on-record DRAM-supply quote, and early review scores. No existing July Steam Machine article; not a duplicate.
concerns: Two of the five sources (xda-developers.com, pcgamesn.com) are off the allowlist. Both are established, reputable outlets and are used for a price-context recap and a review roundup respectively; acceptable as an editorial warning, allowlist left unmodified.

Three subordinate-body attribution/accuracy slips (see factual_accuracy) — each recoverable and honestly summarizable, so APPROVE_WITH_CORRECTIONS rather than REJECT; none touch the headline, summary, or lead.
recommendations: Publish with the corrections record so readers see the ~40% (not 30%) price delta and the two source-attribution clarifications.
Contributor should attribute the SteamOS/Linux detail and the AI/data-center causation to GamersNexus, and recompute the percentage before reusing these framings.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Solid, timely launch report whose central claims (date, four-tier pricing, lottery, memory-shortage cause, above-target price) are all verified against cited snapshots. Three minor subordinate issues are covered by a public corrections trail. APPROVE_WITH_CORRECTIONS.
